To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the oxidation of non‐phenolic substrates by lignin peroxidases and manganese peroxidases is dependent on the presence of Mn(II), while the oxidation of phenols is not.
the three enzymes oxidize phenolic substrates but only MnP requires Mn(II) as a co‐substrate and that the catalytic activity of LiP towards non‐phenolic substrates is repressed by Mn(II).
laccase, MnP and LiP from Phlebia radita oxidized non‐phenolic and phenolic substrates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oxidation of non‐phenolic compounds by LiP and Mn(II)‐dependent oxidation of MnP.
the study of the catalysis of the three enzymes from P. radiata.
the study of the oxidation capacities of laccases, manganese peroxidases and lignin peroxides from Phlebia radita, and the effect of Mn(11) on the catalysis of these enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Mn(III) is the oxidizing agent in the reactions catalyzed by laccase and MnP and Mn(II) is the reducing agent in LiP catalysis.
the oxidation capacities of LiP are restricted to non‐phenolic compounds.
laccase is the only enzyme capable of oxidizing phenolic and non‐phenolic substrates, and that the catalysis of both MnP and LiP is dependent on the presence of Mn(II).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MnP is a Mn(III)‐oxidizing peroxidase, LiP a Mn(II)‐oxidizing peroxygenase and laccase a non‐Mn(II)‐dependent phenol oxidase.
laccase is the main ligninolytic enzyme in the fungus P. radiata and MnP and LiP have minor roles in lignin degradation.
Mn(II) is an important cofactor for MnP and a repressor for the catalysis of LiP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catalytic properties of laccases, MnP and LiP from P. radiata are different from those of their fungal counterparts and may be useful in the bioremediation of industrial effluents.
MnP is a manganese‐containing enzyme and its catalysis requires Mn(II) as a cofactor.
the oxidation capacities of the three enzymes studied are very different and the catalytic mechanisms of these enzymes are not similar.
